parts:
I'm working on a spatio-temporal model almost identical to the form in the paper linked below. 

https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?repid=rep1&type=pdf&doi=8ba35e5d6144e1c7f2ccb65826b2864514ea98e9

The main difference I'd like to implement is to measure the estimated period-over-period change for each node in spatial latent field at each time period, excluding the first time period of course. There is a high degree of heterogeneity in each observation making transformation of the response to period-over-period seem less useful. 

Has anyone done or come across something similar within this framework that I could study?

Hi Finn,

My apologies for the vague description.

I'm possibly misinterpreting an approach or being led astray; I'm growing more doubtful as I grapple with the idea more. Just to clarify and close the loop, in case you have any better ideas.

A simplified version of the idea is conveyed at the link below, on page 16 and 17 (equation 7a, 7b, and 8)
https://www.imf.org/external/pubs/ft/wp/2016/wp16213.pdf

an individual property is represented as i

Current (as shown here https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?repid=rep1&type=pdf&doi=8ba35e5d6144e1c7f2ccb65826b2864514ea98e9):
Price(i) = Beta(s,t) + Beta(attributes)

Ideal (latent price index is the response; we can't create the response in this way due to heterogenous properties/sales and we want to leverage that to measure the latent price index) :
Price(s,t) - Price(s, t-1) = Beta(s,t) + Beta(attributes)

Potential work around (I think this is how I misinterpreted the IMF paper above):
Price(i) = ( Beta(s,t) - Beta(s,t-1) ) + Beta(attributes)
                  ^^ The price index ^^

The latter seems flawed because the Current approach adequately controls for spatial and temporal autocorrelation, and it isn't expected that 
the rate of appreciation/depreciation is a primary driver of the current price; it's just that the rate of appreciation/depreciation is what we're trying to estimate across both space and time. 

The way I'm addressing this now using the Current approach is calculating the index after modeling, using inla.mesh.project for each grouped time period (and mesh location), by converting to a raster (R) then calculating RIndex = Rt - R(t-1).

Thanks for all of your fantastic work!
